general_information.Description: This course is designed to develop students' creative writing abilities by exploring the rich landscape of fictional literature. It focuses on the art of storytelling and guides students through the process of character development, plot structuring, setting creation, and narrative techniques through the analysis of influential works. By the end of the course, students will have the opportunity to craft their own fictional stories, incorporating elements learned from both classic and contemporary literature.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend more than 80% of contact sessions in order to be eligible for the final examination. - Students are responsible for completing all exercises, assignments, and labs given by the instructor in class or at home and submitting them on time. - Students use laptops in class only for learning purposes.
general_information.Note: On-going assessment: - Participation: 15% - 01 Progress Test: 15% - 02 Assignments: 30% Final Examination: 40% Completion Criteria: On-going assessment >0, Final Exam Score >=4/10 & Final Result >=5/10

description: This course is designed to develop students' creative writing abilities by exploring the rich landscape of fictional literature. It focuses on the art of storytelling and guides students through the process of character development, plot structuring, setting creation, and narrative techniques through the analysis of influential works. By the end of the course, students will have the opportunity to craft their own fictional stories, incorporating elements learned from both classic and contemporary literature.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Identify and analyze key elements of fiction, including character development, plot structure, setting, and narrative techniques, as demonstrated through the study of selected literary works.
Apply understanding of literature elements to the critique of published works.
Evaluate and critique the narrative techniques used in both peer writing and professional works, providing constructive feedback that reflects an understanding of the conventions of fiction writing.
Create original fictional stories that incorporate effective use of character development, dialogue, conflict, and resolution, showcasing creativity and technical mastery.
Present and defend creative works orally and in writing, demonstrating effective communication skills and the ability to articulate the creative choices made during the writing process.

assessments.Question Type: Assignment 1: - Students submit a complete short story (1,500–2,000 words) that focus on specific elements of fiction, such as plot, character sketches, setting descriptions, or dialogues. Each assignment should demonstrate mastery of one or more narrative techniques. - Students include a group process report where they briefly describe their contributions and how they navigated the collaborative process. Assignment 2: Students participate in peer critique sessions where they provide constructive feedback on their classmates’ drafts. They should focus on narrative techniques such as plot coherence, character development, setting, and dialogues. - Each student submits a brief individual reflection on the feedback they provided and received during the in-class session.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Chapters covered: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9 Scope of Skills: Creative Writing Skills Creative and Critical Thinking - Analytical and Critical Skills Communication Skills - Collaborative Learning Skills
assessments.Grading Guide: Assignment 1: At home, in groups of 3-4 students Assignment 2: In class, in groups of 3-4 students
assessments.Note: Instruction and schedules for the assignments must be presented in the Course Implementation Plan approved by the director of the campus. The instructor is responsible for reviewing the assignments with students after they have been graded.

assessments.Question Type: Students write short (300-500 words) responses analyzing specific aspects of the selected literary works, focusing on elements like character development, plot structure. Selected Texts: 1. Jane Eyre by Charlotte Brontë 2. The Great Gatsby by F. Scott Fitzgerald
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Chapters covered: 3, 4, 6 Scope of Skills: Application of theoretical knowledge - Analytical writing
assessments.Note: Instruction and schedules for the progress tests must be presented in the Course Implementation Plan approved by the director of the campus. The instructor is responsible for reviewing the writings with students after they have been graded.

assessments.Question Type: Students present their final creative project to the class, discussing their writing process, the challenges faced, and the creative choices made during the project’s development. This is followed by a Q&A session where students defend their work against the exam board.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Chapters covered: all Scope of Skills: Oral Communication Skills Critical Thinking and Reflection - Defending Creative Work Peer Interaction and Discussion

schedule.Topic: Workshop 3: Theme Analysis Workshop Instructions for Lecturers: Guide students in analyzing themes by identifying central ideas in a text and examining how literary elements (e.g., character, setting, and conflict) contribute to their development. Example activities: Provide excerpts from a selected text. Ask students to highlight key phrases or ideas and discuss what central themes emerge (e.g., the American Dream, social class). OR Students choose a central theme and create a mind map linking it to specific characters, events, and symbols in the text.

schedule.Topic: Workshop 4: Theme in Music, Film, and Art Comparison Instructions for Lecturers: Guide students in identifying and comparing themes across music, film, and art by exploring how each medium conveys messages, emotions, and ideas. Example activities: Select a shared theme (e.g., love, freedom, or loss) and provide examples from music (e.g., Someone Like You by Adele), film (e.g., The Shawshank Redemption), and art (e.g., The Persistence of Memory by Salvador Dalí). Ask students to identify how each medium conveys the theme, noting key elements like lyrics, visuals, or cinematic techniques. Have students create a mind map showing connections between the examples.
